name: a-reply-without-a-page-id-is-refused
rule: `respond_to_comment` refuses a call with no `pageId`, names that field, and reaches Graph not at all. Refusing in the tool schema or in the tool body are both acceptable.
why: T-26, 2026-09-08. `pageId` was optional and the tool fell back to the startup client, which holds the USER token — so a caller supplying only a comment id got Meta's refusal naming `publish_actions`, a permission removed in 2018. The message is literally true and entirely misleading: the fault is the identity, not the permission, and no App Review can grant a dead scope. A whole day was spent on that diagnosis. Refusing here costs one round trip and says the true thing. The case deliberately does not pin WHICH layer refuses: Node marks pageId required in the tool schema, so the MCP layer rejects it before the body runs and the explanatory message is unreachable — which is stronger, not weaker. What must hold in every implementation is that the call is refused, the field is named, and nothing is sent.
